title_en: Migration from the Standpoint of the Sharia
body_ar:
إذا كان الإنسان آمنا على نفسه و دينه و خلقه فلا حرج في هجرته لطلب الرزق أو الأمان إلى أي أرض فيها مسلمون يقيمون معه شعائر الدين أما البلاد التي ليس فيها مسلمون أو لا يستطيعون فيها إقامة شعائر الدين كالجمع و الجماعات أو يخالف فيها المسلم على نفسه أو دينه أو خلقه أو أهله و أولاده فلا يحل له المقام فيها بين ظهراني الكفار

و الأولى في واقعنا أن لا يخرج المسلم بالأولاد الصغار إلى تلك الديار و كذلك من لا تؤمن عليها الفتنة من النساء و الله أعلم
body_en:
If a person is secure as to himself, his religion and his character, there is no blame in his migrating in search of livelihood or of safety to any land in which there are Muslims who keep up the observances of the religion together with him. As for countries in which there are no Muslims, or in which they are unable to keep up the observances of the religion — such as the Friday congregational prayers and the prayers in congregation — or in which fear is entertained for the Muslim as to himself, his religion, his character, or his household and his children: it is not lawful for him to take up residence there, in the midst of the unbelievers.

In our present circumstances the preferable course is that a Muslim should not take young children out to those lands, and likewise those women for whom the danger of trial cannot be ruled out. And God knows best.

flags.arabic: فلا يحل له المقام فيها بين ظهراني الكفار
flags.context: the ruling on residing in countries where the religion's observances cannot be kept up
options: it is not lawful for him to take up residence there, in the midst of the unbelievers
it is not permitted for him to remain there among the non-Muslims
residence there among the disbelievers is not lawful for him
flags.note: EDITORIALLY SENSITIVE and a live ruling. 'لا يحل' is the negation of lawfulness, i.e. forbidden (ḥarām), and has not been softened to 'should not'. الكفار is rendered 'the unbelievers', which is what the Arabic says; 'non-Muslims' would soften it and 'infidels' would strengthen it. Published in English in a diaspora context, a ruling that residence in certain non-Muslim countries is unlawful carries real reputational exposure, and the conditions attached to it (no Muslims at all, or inability to perform the congregational prayers, or fear for one's religion or family) are easily lost in quotation. The conditions are load-bearing and must not be dropped in any excerpt.

flags.arabic: أو يخالف فيها المسلم على نفسه أو دينه
flags.context: the third condition that makes residence unlawful
options: read as يُخاف: 'or in which fear is entertained for the Muslim as to himself, his religion…'
read as written, يخالف: 'or in which the Muslim goes against himself, his religion…'
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, recorded not fixed (house rule 11): 'يخالف ... على' is not a possible construction; خاف/يُخاف takes على and gives the standard juristic formula 'يُخاف على نفسه أو دينه'. body_ar preserves the source; body_en follows the only coherent reading. If the misreading stood, the clause would say something quite different about the resident's own conduct rather than about the danger to him, so this should be confirmed with the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: و الأولى في واقعنا أن لا يخرج المسلم بالأولاد الصغار
options: the preferable course is that a Muslim should not take young children out
it is better that a Muslim not take young children out
flags.note: RULING-STRENGTH FLAG. 'الأولى' states what is preferable; its opposite is khilāf al-awlā, which the glossary marks as weaker than makrūh and distinct from it. This paragraph is therefore NOT a prohibition and must not be rendered or excerpted as one. The contrast with 'لا يحل' in the paragraph above is deliberate and has been preserved.

flags.arabic: من لا تؤمن عليها الفتنة من النساء
flags.context: the second category the Sheikh advises against taking
options: those women for whom the danger of trial cannot be ruled out
women who cannot be considered safe from temptation
women in whose case the risk of fitnah is not removed
flags.note: fitnah here is trial or temptation in religion; it is not in the project glossary and its sense shifts across the corpus (sedition, civil strife, temptation). Flagged rather than fixed. The passive 'لا تؤمن' means the danger is not ruled out, which is weaker than asserting that it exists.

translator_notes: A SHORT BUT COMPLETE FATWA: 441 characters, a full ruling with its conditions and a closing 'و الله أعلم'. It is not an audio stub, and a length-based rule would have suppressed it.
'شعائر الدين' rendered 'the observances of the religion'; 'الجمع و الجماعات' are the Friday congregational prayers and the daily prayers in congregation.
'بين ظهراني الكفار' is the prophetic idiom for living in the midst of a people; rendered as the idiom.
No question text is preserved in the record — only the answer. The title is the site's.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date, not the date the opinion was given.
